label: lemthom
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemthom}
		With the same assumptions as in Theorem \ref{thmvn}, there exists an infinite subset $K\subset \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 2},$ such that for all $k\in K$, the integral homology class $k[\Sigma]$ can be represented by a smoothly embedded connected compact submanifold,
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, le us prove the lemma without the connectedness assumption. Let us argue by contradiction. Suppose there exists only a finite subset $F\subset \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 2}$ so that for $k\in F$, the integral homology class has a smoothly embedded representative. By \cite[Theorem II.29]{RT} some multiple of $\left(\prod_{k\in F}k\right)[\Sigma]$ admits a smoothly embedded representative, a contradiction. Here we regard $\prod_{k\in F}k$ as $1$ in case $F$ is empty.
				
Next, let us show that when the codimension of $[\Sigma]$ with respect to the ambient manifold $M$ is at least two, any smoothly embedded representative of $k[\Sigma]$ with finitely many connected components can be made into a connected submanifold by connected sum of submanifolds. The case of $d\ge 2$ is classical \cite{CL} and a detailed write up can be found in \cite[Lemma 2.8.2]{ZLns}. For $d=1$, we utilize a direct construction. For two disjoint smoothly embedded circles $\gamma_1,\gamma_3$, we take another curve $\gamma_2$ that starts from a point on $\gamma_1$ and end at a point on $\gamma_3.$ Let $\gamma_4$ be $\gamma_2$ reversely traversed. Then $\gamma_1+\gamma_2+\gamma_3+\gamma_4$ is homologically equivalent to $\gamma_1+\gamma_3$. As embeddings are generic maps when $d=1<2\le c$ \cite[2.13 Theorem, 2.6 Theorem]{MH}, a generic perturbation of $\gamma_1+\gamma_2+\gamma_3+\gamma_4$ gives a closed embedded circle $\gamma_1\#\gamma_3\in [\gamma_1]+[\gamma_3]\in H_1(M,\mathbb{Z}).$

label: eqsrn
title: Proof
body_md:
Note that regular set of $T$ can have density at most $\frac{n}{2}$. We will prove that if $p\in\operatorname{Supp} \partial S\cap \textnormal{Reg}(T),$ then $\theta_T(p)= \frac{n}{2}.$ 
		
		Since $p$ is in the regular set of $T,$ there exists a neighborhood $\mathbf{B}_r(p)$ in which $T$ restricted to $\mathbf{B}_r(p)$ equals $\theta_T(p) N$ for some smooth submanifold $N$ of $\mathbf{B}_r(p)$, so that in some coordinate system $(x_1,\cdots,x_{d+c})$, $N$ is a smooth ball contained in the $x_1\cdots x_d$-plane. By \cite[Corollary 1.4]{RY}, there exists a $\mathbb{Z}$-flat chain $R$ in $\mathbf{B}_r(p)$ so that
		\begin{align}\label{eqsrn}
			S\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .3pt depth 0pt
			\vrule height .3pt width 5pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits \mathbf{B}_r(p)=nR+\theta_T(p) N,
		\end{align} as a $\mathbb{Z}$-rectifiable current. Here $S\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .3pt depth 0pt
			\vrule height .3pt width 5pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits \mathbf{B}_r(p)$ means $S$ restricted to $\mathbf{B}_r(p).$ Since $S,N$ are both of finite mass, we deduce that $R$ is also of finite mass, thus a $\mathbb{Z}$-rectifiable current by \cite[Section 4.2.16]{HF}.
		
		If $R=0,$ then $\partial S$ restricted to $\mathbf{B}_r(p)$ is empty, as $S$ coincides with $\theta_T(p)N.$ Thus, we only have to deal with the case of $R\not=0.$
		
		Recall Fact \ref{fctcf}.
		There exist a $d$-dimensional rectifiable set $B$, an $\mathcal{H}^d$ measurable simple unit $d$-vector field $\eta$ , so that the action of the current $R$ on differential forms is
		\begin{align*}
			R(\phi)=\int_B\theta_R\phi(\eta) d\mathcal{H}^d(x), 
		\end{align*}
		with $\phi$ any smooth $d$-dimensional form. 
		
		By \cite[page 430]{HF}, the support of $S$ restricted to $\mathbf{B}_r(p)$ is contained in $N,$ thus by (\ref{eqsrn}) the support of $R$ is also contained in $N,$ i.e., $B\subset N.$ This implies that $\eta=\pm \mathbf{T}_x N$ Hausdorff $d$-dimensional a.e.~ Here $\mathbf{T}_x N$ means the unique simple $d$-vector field representing the tangent space at $x$ to $N.$
		
		Thus, we have
		\begin{align*}
			S\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .3pt depth 0pt
			\vrule height .3pt width 5pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits \mathbf{B}_r(p)(\phi)=\int_{N\setminus B}\theta_T(p) \phi(\mathbf{T}_xN)d\mathcal{H}^d(x)+\int_{B} (\theta_T(p)\pm n\theta_R(x))\phi(\mathbf{T}_xN)d\mathcal{H}^d(x).
		\end{align*} 
		By \cite[Section 4.1.28]{HF}, we deduce that
		\begin{align*}
			\mathbf{M}^{\mathbb{Z}}(S\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .3pt depth 0pt
			\vrule height .3pt width 5pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits \mathbf{B}_r(p))=\int_{N\setminus B}\theta_T(p)d\mathcal{H}^d(x)+\int_B |\theta_T(p)\pm n\theta_R(x)|d\mathcal{H}^d(x).
		\end{align*}
		However, since we have $R\not=0$, i.e., $\theta_R(x)$ being a positive integer on $B$ Hausdorff $d$-dimensional a.e.~, and $\theta_T(p)\le \frac{n}{2}$  by \cite[page 430]{HF}, we have 
		\begin{fact}\label{fctdstin}
			The inequality		\begin{align}\label{eqtatr}
				|\theta_T(p)\pm n\theta_R(x)|\ge \frac{n}{2},
			\end{align}holds
			where equality is achieved if and only if $\theta_T(p)=\frac{n}{2},\theta_R(x)=1.$
		\end{fact}	
		Thus, we have
		\begin{align*}
			\mathbf{M}^{\mathbb{Z}}(S\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .3pt depth 0pt
			\vrule height .3pt width 5pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits \mathbf{B}_r(p))\ge \theta_T(p) \mathbf{M}(N)=\mathbf{M}^{\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}}(T\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .3pt depth 0pt
			\vrule height .3pt width 5pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits \mathbf{B}_r(p)). 
		\end{align*} By Fact \ref{fctrmn}, we  have\begin{align*}
			\mathbf{M}^{\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}}(T\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .3pt depth 0pt
			\vrule height .3pt width 5pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits \mathbf{B}_r(p))=	\mathbf{M}^{\mathbb{Z}}(S\mathop{\hbox{\vrule height 7pt width .3pt depth 0pt
			\vrule height .3pt width 5pt depth 0pt}}\nolimits \mathbf{B}_r(p)). 
		\end{align*}
		In other words, equality holds in (\ref{eqtatr}) Hausdorff $d$-dimensional a.e.~ on $B.$ By Fact \ref{fctdstin}, we deduce that
		$$\theta_T(p)=\frac{n}{2},\theta_R(x)=1,$$ on $B$ Hausdorff $d$-dimensional a.e.~ Thus $\partial S$ intersect $\operatorname{Reg} T$ at $\theta_T=\frac{n}{2}$ and we are done.

label: lemsingt
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemsingt}
	Suppose $T$ is a $d$-dimensional  $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$-area-minimizing $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$-	flat chain on a not necessarily compact $(d+c)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(M^{d+c},h)$ with possibly non-zero boundary $\partial T$.	Then	$$\operatorname{Sing} T\cap (\operatorname{Supp}\partial T)^\complement\cap \{\theta_T(p,h)<\frac{n}{2}\}$$ has Hausdorff dimension at most $(d-2).$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Recall Section \ref{ssas}. Since $\theta_T(p,h)$ is an upper-semicontinuous function of $p,$ the set $\{\theta_T(p,h)<\frac{n}{2}\}$ is open. By \cite[Theorem 1.7]{DHMS}, the $d$-th stratum of the Almgren stratification of $\operatorname{Sing} T\cap (\operatorname{Supp}\partial T)^\complement\cap \{\theta_T(p,h)<\frac{n}{2}\}$ is of Hausdorff dimension at most $(d-2)$. On the other hand, by \cite[Lemma 8.6]{DHMS}, for any point $p$ in the $(d-1)$-th stratum of the Almgren stratification of $\operatorname{Sing} T\cap (\operatorname{Supp}\partial T)^\complement\cap \{\theta_T(p,h)<\frac{n}{2}\},$ we have $\theta_T(p,h)\ge\frac{n}{2}$, so the $(d-1)$-th stratum of the Almgren stratification of $\operatorname{Sing} T\cap W\cap \{\theta_T(p,h)<\frac{n}{2}\}$ is empty. By Fact \ref{fctas}, we are done.

label: fctbd
title: Fact
body_md:
\label{fctbd}
Assume that $S$ is a $d$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}$-rectifiable current on a not necessarily compact $(d+c)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M^{d+c}.$ If $$\operatorname{Supp}\partial S\subset W\cup O,$$ with $W$ and $W\cup O$ closed, $O$ disjoint from $W$ and $O$ having Hausdorff dimension at most $(d-2)$, then we have $$\operatorname{Supp} \partial S\subset W.$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Fact \ref{fctrmn}, $\partial S$ is a $\mathbb{Z}$-rectifiable current.
 By the definition of support \cite[Section 4.1.1 p.344]{HF}, it suffices to prove that for every point $p\in M\setminus W$, there is a neighborhood $U(p)$ in which $T(\phi)=0$ with $\phi$ any smooth $d$-form vanishing outside of $U(p).$ Recall Fact \ref{fctcf}. We have
\begin{align*}
	\partial T(\phi)=&\int_{\operatorname{Rect} \partial T}\theta_{\partial T}\phi(\eta)d\mathcal{H}^{d-1}\\
	=&\int_{\operatorname{Rect} \partial T\cap O}\theta_{\partial T}\phi(\eta)d\mathcal{H}^{d-1}+\int_{\operatorname{Rect}  {\partial T}\cap W}\theta_T\phi(\eta)d\mathcal{H}^{d-1}\\
	=&0+0,
\end{align*}
 where at the last step we used $O$ having Hausdorff dimension at most $(d-2)$ and $\phi$ vanishing on $W$. We are done.

title: Proof
body_md:
First, $W$ admits a finite triangulation (\cite[7.4 Theorem]{BPhs} for subanalytic $W$ and \cite{SCtr} for smooth $W$). Next, there is no $d$-dimensional simplices, so there is non-nontrivial exact $(d-1)$-dimensional chains. Thus, any homology class of $H_{d-1}(W,R)$ has a unique representative by a simplicial cycle. This means that the group $H_{d-1}(W,R)$ is a subgroup of the finitely generated abelian group of $R$-simplicial $d$-dimensional chains in $W$. By \cite[Proposition 4.52]{AKba} $H_{d-1}(W,R)$ is finitely generated. When $R=\mathbb{Z}$ or $\mathbb{R}$, the group of $R$-simplicial chains is free, so its subgroup $H_{d-1}(W,R)$ is also free \cite[Theorem 4.55]{AKba}. We are done with the first bullet and the second bullet.
			
			For the third bullet, as $\partial T=0$, by Fact \ref{fctct}, every $R$-flat cycle is represented by an simplicial $R$-chain and then apply the second bullet. 
			
			The fourth bullet and the last bullet follows from the third bullet and the second bullet.

body_md:
The lemma combines several results of Yongsheng Zhang's thesis \cite{YZt} and published in \cite{YZj,YZa}. Take a tubular neighborhood $U(N)$ of $N$ inside $M.$
The first bullet is \cite[Lemma 3.1]{YZj} applied to $U(N)$ and $M$. The second to the fourth bullet come from \cite[Sections 3.3, 3.4]{YZa}. The last bullet follows from \cite[Lemma 2.12]{ZLa}. For an alternative proof the last bullet, by \cite[Fact 7.0.6]{ZLns} $\pi^\ast_N\operatorname{dvol}_N$ is a calibration form on $U(N)$ implies that $\pi$ is a $d$-dimensional area-non-increasing map from $U(N)$ to $N$, i.e., \begin{align}\label{eqani}
		\mathbf{M}^R(\pi_\ast T)\le \mathbf{M}^R(T),
	\end{align} for $R=\mathbb{Z},$ or $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2 }$ and $T$ any $R$-flat chains supported in $U(N).$ For any $R$-flat chain $N'$ homologous to $N$ in $U(N)$, we necessarily have $\pi_\ast N'=N$ since $\pi$ is a deformation retract. By (\ref{eqani}), we are done.

\label{lemssp}
	Using the same notation as in Fact \ref{fctrmn},  $S$ as a Federer's ``representative" modulo $n$ is unique. In other words, if $S'$ is another Federer's ``representative" modulo $n$ of $T$, then we have	$S=S'$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: First,  $S^{\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}}=(S')^{\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}}=T$ implies $(S'-S)^{\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}}=0$.  As $S$ and $S'$ has the same support and they both have boundaries supported in $W$, they must have the same regular set $$\operatorname{Reg} S=\operatorname{Reg} S'=\operatorname{Reg} S\cap \operatorname{Reg} S'.$$ In each connected component of $\operatorname{Reg} S\cap \operatorname{Reg} S'$, $S'-S$ equals a smooth submanifold counted with multiplicity divisible by $n.$  by (\ref{indst}), $S$ and $S'$ has density strictly less than $\frac{n}{2}$ Hausdorff $d$-dimensional a.e.~. Thus, $S-S'$ has density strictly less than $n$ Hausdorff $d$-dimensional a.e.~. 	This implies that $S$ and $S'$ coincides on their regular set. Since $\operatorname{Sing} S\setminus W=\operatorname{Sing} S'\setminus W=\operatorname{Sing} $ has Hausdorff dimension at most $(d-2)$, we deduce that $S=S'.$

label: eqsfs
title: Proof
body_md:
The class $2[\Sigma]$ always admits a connected embedded smooth complex algebraic subvariety $N$ as a representative. For instance, one can take Fermat hypersurfaces in an equator $\mathbb{CP}^{\frac{d}{2}+1}$ of $\mathbb{CP}^{\frac{d+c}{2}}.$ Then by \cite[page 70 Example I]{HL}, $N$ is $\mathbb{Z}$-area-minimizing in the Fubini-Study metric $g_{FS}$ and calibrated by the form $\frac{1}{(d/2)!}\omega^d,$ where $\omega$ is the standard Kahler form in the Fubini-Study metric. Let $\beta$ be a smooth function on $\mathbb{CP}^{\frac{d}{2}+1}$ such that $\beta\ge 1$ and $\beta^{-1}(1)=N.$ Since $\beta g_{FS}\ge g_{FS}$ as quadratic forms, by the definition of comass in (\ref{defncms}), in metric $\beta g_{FS},$ the form $\frac{1}{(d/2)!}\omega^d$ still calibrates $N$. This implies that 
		\begin{align}\label{eqsfs}
			\left\lVert[\Sigma]\right\rVert_{\beta g_{FS}}^{\mathbb{R}}=\frac{1}{2}\left\lVert2[\Sigma]\right\rVert_{\beta g_{FS}}^{\mathbb{R}}=\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{M}_{\beta g_{FS}}^{\mathbb{Z}}(N).
		\end{align}  Since $\frac{1}{(d/2)!}\omega^d$ have comass $1$ in $\beta g_{FS}$ only on $N,$ by the constancy theorem \cite[Section 4.9]{FMgmt}, any integral current calibrated by $\frac{1}{(d/2)!}\omega^d$ in $\beta g_{FS}$ must be an integer multiple of $N$. As $[\Sigma]$ is not a torsion class, we deduce that 
		\begin{fact}\label{fctnc}
			$N$ is the unique $\mathbb{Z}$-rectifiable current in $2[\Sigma]$ calibrated by $\frac{1}{(d/2)!}\omega^d$.
		\end{fact} If $\left\lVert[\Sigma]\right\rVert^{\mathbb{R}}_{\beta g_{FS}}=\left\lVert[\Sigma]\right\rVert^{\mathbb{Z}}_{\beta g_{FS}}$, then by (\ref{eqsfs}), any element $T\in\mathbf{MIN}_{\beta g_{FS}}^{\mathbb{Z}}([\Sigma])$ must satisfy $\mathbf{M}_{\beta g_{FS}}^{\mathbb{Z}}(T)=\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{M}_{\beta g_{FS}}^{\mathbb{Z}}(N).$ Thus, we have $2T\in 2[\Sigma]$ and $2T$ has the same area as $N.$ By Fact \ref{fcthl}, this implies that $2T$ is also calibrated by $\frac{1}{(d/2)!}\omega^d$, which contradicts Fact \ref{fctnc}. Replacing $\beta$ by $1+\epsilon(\beta-1)$ for positive $\epsilon\to0$. We are done.
